trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right, down, up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going down would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes left.
Cell (5,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Going up, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,1). So the line goes left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (right from number 1) was wrong. Next I'll try down.
Going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going right would leave both cell (4,6) and cell (6,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Going right would wall in number 8, the last number. So the line goes up.
Going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,1). So the line goes left.
Going up would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (1,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.

Going down would force the line onto number 7 before its turn; going through the portal to (6,2) would leave both cell (6,1) and cell (6,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes right.
Going down would leave both cell (2,5) and cell (3,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes through the portal to (3,2).
Cell (3,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (4,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (5,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
